- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially in early/medium horizon.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if recent price is trending up.
- Overshoots after sharp spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 1-2 days) are common; cap forecast at 1-2% above peak or use moving average to smooth.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1-2% per day until convergence.
- Horizon-specific: 10-14 day forecasts often overestimate; 20+ day forecasts underperform; adjust downward for longer horizons if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history shows 3+ consecutive 0.00 values, model tends to ignore trend; force a slight upward bias to avoid underestimating rebound.
